fixes.explanation: Six it is, friend. Ezekiel sees six men coming from the Upper Gate, which faces north, and each one has a weapon of slaughter in his hand (Ezekiel 9:2). Six men, six weapons, and a scene this heavy. I'm keeping my apron straight.

Close, but the text says six, not four. Ezekiel sees six men coming from the Upper Gate, each with a weapon of slaughter in his hand (Ezekiel 9:2). Four would make a smaller group than the one in the verse. Here, it's six.

Twelve would be a whole crowd, friend, but the text says six. Ezekiel sees six men coming from the Upper Gate, each with a weapon of slaughter in his hand (Ezekiel 9:2). Twelve is a bigger group than the one in the verse. Here, it's six.

A ram's horn would make some noise, but that's not what he carries. The man clothed in linen has a writing kit at his side (Ezekiel 9:2). No horn is mentioned anywhere in this verse. Just the writing kit.

The altar is in the scene, since the men stand beside the bronze altar (Ezekiel 9:2), but the mark isn't about offerings. The LORD says it goes on the foreheads of the men "…sighing and groaning over all the abominations committed there." (Ezekiel 9:4). Offerings aren't mentioned in that verse. The men are described as sighing and groaning over what was committed in the city.
Borders aren't mentioned in this verse, friend. God says, "Now begin at My sanctuary." (Ezekiel 9:6). The text says they began with the elders who were before the temple. That's where the six start.
